liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Truckin'** (1 review, 2 other sources): Truckin' is singled out as strong, along with the Alabama Getaway/Johnny B. Goode pairing; A slight Spanish jam follows Truckin' [5][6][20]
- **Uncle John's Band** (2 reviews): Uncle John's Band coming out of Space signals something good; a brief Spanish jam follows, on Cinco de Mayo; The last section of Uncle John's Band was especially terrific in the second set [15][18]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): The jam between Scarlet and Fire is sublime, and the first guitar break in Fire is epic, ending in a band and crowd freak-out; Jerry fries the first guitar break in the jam into Fire [17][25]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The Scarlet/Fire pairing is described as standard great [15]
- **Feel Like a Stranger** (1 review): Feel Like a Stranger ran long and felt very strange to the reviewer [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-05-05 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **gd81-05-05 s1t02 Feel Like A Stranger**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **gd81-05-05 s1t03 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **gd81-05-05 s1t04 El Paso**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **gd81-05-05 s1t05 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **gd81-05-05 s1t06 CC Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **gd81-05-05 s1t07 Brown Eyed Women**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **gd81-05-05 s1t08 Passenger**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-05-05.143044.senn421.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 170 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1981-05-05.150659.cm.fob.nak700.miller.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 175 min [5]
- **gd1981-05-05.150617.cm.fob.nak700.miller.flac24**: source not stated; 21 songs; 175 min [6]
- **gd1981-05-05.152447.beyer201-prescott.holbrook.flac2448**: soundboard; 22 songs; 157 min [8]
- **gd81-05-05.nak300-mow.ford.28356.sbeok.flac**: audience recording; 22 songs; 164 min; rated 4/5 by 19 [11]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has excellent sound, with Phil's bass undercurrents rolling in relentlessly; The recording is described as incredibly clear and sweet [16][24]
- **gd81-05-05.wise.clugston.8595.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 168 min; rated 4.44/5 by 9 [12]. Said about its sound: Recording quality brings out the players' communication in the Scarlet>Fire jam; best heard on headphones [17]

## Around the show

- Reviewer stood in the second row on Phil's side [17]
- At showtime, staff drew curtains over the big hall windows to darken the room [18]
- Reviewer was 15 at the show, remembers the scene outside and inside the civic center, and now lives near the venue [21]
- The short Spanish jam foreshadows the full Spanish jam the next night, which is generally thought to be that jam's return [15]
- The second set is among the finest from the early 80s, with one climactic moment after another in the first seventy minutes [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-05-05.143044.senn421.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Jim Wise's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII-C90)(located at the soundboard); Transfer Info: Master… [1]. Also: A Doug Lamarre and Rob Berger Arista mic source supplies a 31-second patch in Drums [1]
- **gd1981-05-05.150659.cm.fob.nak700.miller.flac16**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi CM700 > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-S/Dolby B) [5]. Also: Sennheiser 421 cassette master supplies patches; Jim Wise and Scott Clugston provided the patch source [5]
- **gd1981-05-05.150617.cm.fob.nak700.miller.flac24**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi CM700 > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-S/Dolby B) [6]. Also: Sennheiser 421 cassette master supplies patches; Jim Wise and Scott Clugston provided the patch source [6]
- **gd1981-05-05.152447.beyer201-prescott.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by David Prescott; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: Beyer m201c Recorder: Sony TCD5 Maxell UDXLII 90's Location: tape says: 'Mics in hat 2nd row reserved even with sbd' Meaning about 75 feet from stacks 5-7 feet… [8]. Also: Master missing 1 minute 25 seconds at the end, spliced from another source, shnID 102023; Copy may derive from a master where about seven minutes around Scarlet and Drums were cut to save tape [8]
- **gd81-05-05.nak300-mow.ford.28356.sbeok.flac**: taped by Doug Mow; transferred by Doug Mow; source: Audience Recording: 2 Nak 300 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell XLIIS tape (Jeff Silberman's guns on Howard Shame's bodies) [11]
- **gd81-05-05.wise.clugston.8595.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [12]
